inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted per H1 FY2026 interim (period ended 30 June 2026), latest available. Held FLAT: SBC is small (~0.5% of revenue) and fully expensed in the flows; GEG has never run an open-market buyback program (trustee purchases for the award scheme only, HK$16-26m/yr) -- dividends are the sole capital-return mechanism.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash-flow statement (Share-based compensation add-back). No equity-award-tax withholding line disclosed -- Hong Kong/Macau filers do not carry the US-style net-share-settlement withholding tax; sbc_incl_equity_taxes = sbc.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-06-30 (H1 FY2026 interim, for net debt/cash/shares); FY2025 (2025-12-31) for the income-statement and cash-flow base year
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% built on HKD/USD-linked risk-free (HKD effectively pegged to USD via the Linked Exchange Rate System) plus an equity risk premium above the US-tech default to reflect Macau-specific regulatory/concession risk, geographic concentration in Mainland China, and gaming-sector cyclicality. Held equal across all three scenarios -- cyclicality and concession risk are priced in the flows (scenario-specific growth/margin paths and probability weights), not stacked again in the discount rate (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt-like: lease liabilities (HK$659.5m total, FY2025) are immaterial (<2% of net cash, <0.5x annual EBITDA) and are NOT added to net_debt or deducted from flows -- reported FCF already reflects only the small financing-activity lease payment (HK$93.6m FY2025, principal+interest), which is de minimis relative to the ~HK$36bn net cash pile and HK$14.5bn EBITDA. No adjustment made; immateriality documented rather than a formal treatment-B build.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (HK$488m equity, ~HK$46-58m annual profit share on HK$10.7-10.9bn group net income, <1%). Flows use NetProfitAttributable-consistent margins implicitly via the EBITDA-down component build; no separate NCI deduction needed given the scale.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'), read owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md. GEG is a Macau casino/integrated-resort concessionaire -- high structural cyclicality (COVID-era revenue collapsed from HK$52bn FY2019 to HK$11.5bn FY2022) now in a policy-supported recovery/growth phase (record 2025 Macau visitation, Capella opened Feb-2026, StarWorld renovation completing Q1-2027, Cotai Phase 4 targeted 2027). FY2025 is treated as the base year rather than a trough or a peak: it is a genuine post-recovery new-normal level (record visitation, normalized EBITDA growth of 5% after stripping ~HK$1.48bn of favorable gaming-luck variance from the 19% reported growth), not a COVID trough requiring mid-cycle normalization upward, nor a luck-inflated peak requiring markdown (the luck adjustment is already visible in normalized vs reported EBITDA and is reflected in the moderate Year-1 growth assumption below rather than a separate haircut). MAJOR TAX FINDING: GEG's gaming profits are exempt from Macau Complementary Tax for five years from the 2023 assessment year (through 2027) under a Macau Government despatch tied to the 2022 concession renewal; FY2025 effective cash tax rate was only 1.9% (HK$208.8m charge / HK$10,928.8m pretax). The Group is also now in scope of OECD Pillar Two (15% global minimum tax, effective 1 Jan 2025 in Hong Kong) though management currently assesses no top-up provision is required. The cash tax rate is ramped from ~2% toward 15% (Pillar Two floor) over years 1-4 as the gaming exemption lapses after 2027 -- carrying the ~2% rate forward in perpetuity would be a material, avoidable overstatement (owner-fcf.md section 2b). NON-OPERATING ASSET / MATCHING INCOME: GEG holds 'cash and liquid investments' of HK$37.7bn (H1 FY2026) that is much broader than balance-sheet cash (HK$15.7bn) -- it also includes HK$17.1bn of listed debt securities at amortised cost (interest-generating) and HK$5.5bn of financial assets at FVOCI (predominantly a 5.2m-share Wynn Resorts stake, fair value HK$4.0bn, generating small dividend income). Net_debt/cash in this file uses the FULL HK$37.7bn 'cash and liquid investments' figure as the matching asset, and total interest income (HK$1,210m FY2025, spanning bank deposits + amortised-cost securities) plus Wynn dividend income is stripped from owner FCF -- per the matching-asset rule, every stripped income stream's source asset must be in the bridge. Leases and NCI are immaterial and require no special adjustment (documented above rather than silently ignored). Historical growth CAGRs are heavily distorted by the COVID collapse and recovery (3yr/5yr revenue CAGR off the FY2020-22 troughs are +31-63%, pure recovery noise) -- FY2019-to-FY2025 CAGRs (a full pre-COVID-peak-to-now cycle) were used as the conservative anchor instead: revenue roughly flat (-0.9%/yr, reflecting the VIP-to-mass mix shift since 2019 dragging on gross gaming revenue even as visitation and mass volumes are at records) and equity +2.1%/yr. Forward growth is instead built bottom-up from company-specific catalysts (Capella ramp, Horizon Plus premium salon expansion, StarWorld renovation completion, Phase 4) and Macau industry GGR consensus (CLSA: continued mid-single-digit growth 2026-2027), not extrapolated from the distorted CAGRs.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_6yr_cagr_precovid_peak (FY2019 pre-COVID peak to FY2025, the only window that spans a full boom-bust-recovery cycle without terminating inside the COVID trough or the post-trough recovery surge)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr/5yr revenue and FCF CAGRs (+31% to +63%) are COVID-recovery artifacts, not organic growth, and are NOT used as the growth anchor -- see inputs.notes. The equity CAGR itself is subdued (2.1%/yr) mainly because GEG paid out the large majority of post-COVID earnings as dividends (retaining little) while absorbing FY2020-2022 losses directly against equity; it understates the underlying earnings-power recovery. Forward scenario growth is instead built bottom-up from company-specific catalysts and Macau industry GGR consensus, not mechanically extrapolated from any single historical CAGR.

base.narrative: GEG's Macau recovery continues on its current, policy-supported trajectory: Capella ramps through its first full year, Horizon Plus premium-mass salon expansion (6->10) continues to capture high-value customers, and the StarWorld renovation completes on schedule (~Q1 2027), removing its current EBITDA drag and lifting the Peninsula property's margin. Macau GGR grows mid-single-digit industry-wide per CLSA/consensus, with GEG holding its ~20% share (neither closing nor materially widening the gap to Sands China). Phase 4 capex peaks over FY2026-2027 (~HK$20bn remaining, targeted completion 2027) then steps down sharply once complete, with the new capacity (five luxury hotel brands, theatre, casino) beginning to contribute incremental revenue from around year 3-4 -- captured here as a moderating but still-positive growth rate rather than a discrete step-up, since ramp timing/demand-absorption for the new supply is genuinely uncertain (bear case flags this explicitly). The temporary Macau Complementary Tax exemption on gaming profits lapses after the 2027 assessment year and the cash tax rate ramps to the OECD Pillar Two 15% floor by year 4.

bull.narrative: Phase 4 pulls forward and ramps faster than expected (management has signaled ambition to accelerate the timeline), the five new ultra-luxury hotel brands and expanded casino floor successfully absorb incremental premium-mass demand rather than cannibalizing existing properties, and GEG closes rather than cedes market share to Sands China as Capella, Horizon Plus and the completed StarWorld renovation combine to lift the premium-mass mix further and expand margins toward the mid-30s%. Mainland Chinese visitation and spending power continue to strengthen (visa facilitation, record international arrivals) well beyond current consensus, and the Macau government extends or renews favorable tax treatment (Shareholder Dividend Tax Agreement, gaming exemption) given GEG's scale of non-gaming investment commitment, keeping the effective tax ramp slightly gentler than the base case. WACC ticks down modestly on reduced perceived regulatory/concentration risk as the concession's non-gaming commitments are demonstrably met.

bear.narrative: Sands China's share gains continue to widen (the ~6pp Q1 2026 gap keeps growing) as GEG's single-jurisdiction, single-country-of-customer-origin concentration proves a structural disadvantage against better-diversified and better-capitalized Cotai peers. Mainland Chinese consumer weakness, a renewed anti-corruption/capital-control campaign, or adverse travel-policy shifts (all recurring historical risks for Macau VIP/premium gaming) dent premium-mass and VIP momentum just as Phase 4's ~HK$20bn of incremental capacity comes online, producing a demand-absorption shortfall that compresses margins (StarWorld-style renovation drag persists longer than guided, event-driven disruptions like the 2026 World Cup recur) rather than lifting them. The temporary gaming tax exemption is not extended, Pillar Two top-up exposure proves larger than management's current assessment, and a higher effective cash tax rate (17% terminal) combines with a lower terminal growth and cap multiple to reflect a structurally slower-growing, more heavily taxed Macau gaming market going forward.

scenario_narratives.base: Continued, policy-supported Macau recovery at industry-consensus mid-single-digit GGR growth; GEG holds its ~20% share as Capella, Horizon Plus and the StarWorld renovation completion support premium-mass momentum; Phase 4 capex peaks over FY2026-2027 then steps down; the temporary gaming-tax exemption lapses after 2027 and the cash tax rate ramps to the 15% Pillar Two floor.
scenario_narratives.bull: Phase 4 accelerates and successfully absorbs new premium-mass demand, GEG closes the share gap to Sands China, margins expand toward the mid-30s% as the premium mix deepens, and favorable Macau tax treatment persists somewhat longer than the base case assumes.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sands China's share lead keeps widening, Mainland Chinese demand or travel-policy conditions weaken (a recurring historical risk for Macau VIP/premium gaming), Phase 4's new capacity is not fully absorbed and compresses rather than expands margins, and the gaming tax exemption is not extended while Pillar Two top-up exposure proves larger than currently assessed.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the 15% house default (at 25%) because Macau gaming has a well-documented history of severe macro/policy shocks outside GEG's control (2014-15 anti-corruption campaign, 2020-2022 COVID closures) and GEG carries zero geographic diversification outside Macau -- a bear axis (Mainland Chinese demand/policy shock, continued share loss to Sands, Phase 4 demand-absorption shortfall) is a real, recurring pattern for this specific industry, not a generic downside. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (from the 35% default) because the bull case needs several distinct things to go right simultaneously (Phase 4 acceleration AND successful demand absorption AND closing the Sands share gap AND extended favorable tax treatment) rather than one clean catalyst. Base at 50% reflects that the current recovery trajectory (record 2025/2026 visitation, Capella ramping, StarWorld renovation on schedule) is the best single point estimate.

valuation_philosophy.summary: GEG is valued via a 10-year owner-FCF component DCF (routed as a non-US, cyclical operating company under the dcf-methods skill). A 10-year horizon is used because the EBITDA margin is still normalizing (StarWorld renovation completing Q1 2027) and the cash tax rate is still ramping off a temporary, expiring exemption -- a 5-year horizon would capitalize an immature margin and an unsustainably low tax rate in perpetuity. FY2025 is used as the base year on the view that it represents a genuine post-COVID new-normal (record Macau visitation, normalized EBITDA growth of 5% once the ~HK$1.48bn gaming-luck benefit is stripped out) rather than either a trough needing markdown or a luck-inflated peak needing a separate haircut -- the luck effect is instead reflected in a moderate (not extrapolated-from-reported-growth) Year-1 growth assumption. The single largest driver of the valuation beyond revenue growth is the cash tax ramp: GEG's FY2025 effective cash tax rate of just 1.9% reflects a temporary Macau gaming-profit exemption expiring after the 2027 assessment year, and carrying that rate forward would materially overstate intrinsic value -- the base case ramps to 15% (the OECD Pillar Two global minimum, now in force for Hong Kong-headquartered groups) by year 4. The ~HK$36bn net cash position (using the full 'cash and liquid investments' figure, not just balance-sheet cash, to match the stripped interest/dividend income) is a major share of enterprise value and reflects a decade of strong post-COVID cash generation with minimal debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Phase 4 demand-absorption risk: ~HK$20bn of remaining capex adds significant new luxury room/casino/entertainment capacity by ~2027, and whether Mainland Chinese and international demand growth absorbs it at attractive returns (versus cannibalizing existing GEG properties or sector-wide oversupply as Sands and other concessionaires expand under the same 2022 concession mandates) is genuinely uncertain and is the main base-vs-bull-vs-bear swing factor.

Tax-rate normalization timing and magnitude: the model assumes the Macau gaming-profit exemption is not extended past 2027 and ramps to the 15% Pillar Two floor by year 4 -- if extended (as GCSA has already applied for regarding the related Shareholder Dividend Tax Agreement), intrinsic value would be understated; if Pillar Two top-up exposure proves larger than management currently assesses, it could be understated the other way.

Relative market-share trajectory versus Sands China: a continued widening of the GGR share gap (already ~6pp in Q1 2026) would pressure GEG's growth below even the bear case if it reflects a structural rather than cyclical disadvantage.

Mainland Chinese macro and travel-policy conditions: GEG has zero revenue diversification outside Macau/Mainland-China-sourced visitation, unlike Sands, Wynn or MGM's US and other-Asia exposure -- this is the dominant macro risk axis for the entire investment case.

Gaming-luck (hold-rate) variance makes any single year's reported EBITDA growth an unreliable read of underlying momentum -- normalized figures (which the model's Year-1 growth assumption is calibrated to, not reported growth) are the more reliable anchor but are themselves management-disclosed rather than independently audited.
